Fit TF–IDF once per category using permitted titles/descriptions; proposed reproducible settings: float32, lowercase, word unigrams, max_features=20,000, min_df=1, smooth_idf=True, norm='l2'. Save vocabulary, IDF, item mapping and configuration. Keep vectors in CSR; normalized dot products give cosine similarities. Empty documents remain zero vectors; handle an entirely empty vocabulary explicitly. Compute sequence-local similarities using sparse products, avoiding a dense full-catalog similarity matrix. [scikit-learn documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html)

Implementation derivation: for prefix ending at t, define support s[t,i]=max({S[i,j]: j≤t, |i−j|≥3, item_i≠item_j}∪{0}), for i≤t. Mask padding, nearby positions and repeated item IDs in S[B,L,L], replacing invalid similarities with zero. Then `S.cummax(dim=-1).values` stores support indexed [batch,i,t]; transpose and mask i>t before pooling. This computes maxima in O(BL²), versus O(BL³) for independently scanning every prefix/item/witness triple. Weighted pooling costs O(BL²d); streaming successive columns with `maximum` reduces support-state storage to O(BL), provided similarity columns are also streamed. These are complexity deductions, not measured speedups. [PyTorch cummax](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cummax.html)

Normalize supported weights by their sum; when that sum is zero, explicitly fall back to the mean of valid prefix embeddings, returning zero for an empty prefix. Share preprocessing, masks, truncation, positions and pooling code between training and the predictor writer. Compare streamed/vectorized results against a small naive reference, including left padding, repeated IDs, empty text and short prefixes. Preserve seeds 0/42 and category routing; assess improvements only through the specified macro validation HR@10.
